hello.legal: Reminder: only audit a network you are authorised to audit.
legal.confirm: I confirm I am authorised to audit the network of site "{site}".
legal.warning: Scanning a network without permission is illegal, in Belgium and elsewhere. Only audit networks you own or for which the owner has given you explicit permission.
netinfo.no_subnet: No subnet to suggest: this machine is not connected to any IPv4 local network.
netinfo.reduced: — larger network, reduced to this machine's /24
ports.full_confirm: The full profile tests all 65535 ports on each device: it is slow and more visible on the network. Continue?
ports.summary: {open} open port(s) on {hosts} device(s) in {seconds} s.
report.authorized_text: On {date}, the technician confirmed being authorised to audit this network.
report.confidential: Confidential document: it describes the network infrastructure and its weaknesses. Share it only with the people concerned.
report.limits: Limits: the audit observes the network from one computer, without credentials or special rights. It only sees services reachable from that computer and does not replace a penetration test. Devices that were off or isolated during the audit do not appear.
report.risk_text.high: At least one critical issue exposes the network to serious risk: it should be addressed without delay.
report.risk_text.low: No critical issue or warning was found: the network shows good hygiene on the items checked.
report.risk_text.medium: No critical issue was found, but several settings should be corrected to reduce risk.
report.summary_changes: Since the audit of {date}: {new} new device(s) ({unknown} unidentified), {gone} device(s) gone and {opened} newly opened port(s).
report.summary_findings: The analysis reports {critical} critical issue(s), {warning} warning(s) and {info} remark(s).
report.summary_intro: On {date}, the network of site "{site}" ({ranges}) was audited: {devices} device(s) were found, offering {ports} network service(s) in total.
report.title: Network audit report
rule.database_exposed.explain: A database ({service}) accepts connections from the local network; if poorly protected, its data is exposed.
rule.database_exposed.fix: Restrict access to the machines that need it (firewall) and check authentication.
rule.database_exposed.title: Database reachable on the network (port {port})
rule.docker_api.explain: This port gives full control of the machine to anyone who can connect to it.
rule.docker_api.fix: Close port 2375 or switch to TLS with client certificates (port 2376).
rule.docker_api.title: Unprotected Docker API (port 2375)
rule.ftp_plain.explain: FTP file transfer sends credentials and files in clear text over the network.
rule.ftp_plain.fix: Replace it with SFTP or FTPS, or disable the service if unused.
rule.ftp_plain.title: Unencrypted FTP (port {port})
rule.http_admin_plain.explain: The page "{title}" appears to ask for credentials, but the connection is not encrypted: the password can be intercepted on the network.
rule.http_admin_plain.fix: Enable HTTPS on the device and disable plain HTTP access.
rule.http_admin_plain.title: Admin interface without HTTPS (port {port})
rule.outdated.explain: This service announces {product} {version}, an old version that likely has known security flaws.
rule.outdated.fix: Update the device or software to a maintained version.
rule.outdated.title: Outdated software: {product} {version}
rule.rdp_open.explain: Remote Desktop allows logging into this PC from the network; it is a frequent target of password attacks.
rule.rdp_open.fix: Disable it if unused; otherwise restrict it to specific machines, require Network Level Authentication and strong passwords.
rule.rdp_open.title: Remote Desktop (RDP) reachable
rule.smb_v1.explain: SMBv1 is an old version of Windows file sharing, exploited by ransomware such as WannaCry.
rule.smb_v1.fix: Disable SMBv1 on the device and update any equipment that depends on it.
rule.smb_v1.title: File sharing over SMBv1
rule.snmp_public.explain: The device discloses configuration information to anyone asking with the default "public" password.
rule.snmp_public.fix: Change the SNMP community, switch to SNMPv3 or disable SNMP if unused.
rule.snmp_public.title: SNMP answers with the "public" community
rule.ssh_v1.explain: The SSH server announces version {version}, which allows the old, long-broken SSH-1 protocol.
rule.ssh_v1.fix: Update the device and disable SSH-1.
rule.ssh_v1.title: SSH still accepts protocol 1
rule.telnet.explain: Telnet allows remote control of the device, but everything travels unencrypted, including the password: anyone on the network can read it.
rule.telnet.fix: Disable Telnet and use SSH or the HTTPS web interface instead.
rule.telnet.title: Telnet open on port {port}
rule.tls_expired.explain: This service's security certificate expired on {date}: browsers show warnings and users get used to ignoring them.
rule.tls_expired.title: Expired certificate (port {port})
rule.tls_expiring.explain: This service's certificate expires in {days} day(s), on {date}.
rule.tls_expiring.title: Certificate expiring soon (port {port})
rule.tls_old.explain: The service accepts {version}, an encryption version no longer considered secure.
rule.tls_old.fix: Update the device and allow only TLS 1.2 and 1.3.
rule.tls_old.title: Obsolete encryption {version} (port {port})
rule.tls_self_signed.explain: The service uses a certificate it signed itself: the connection is encrypted, but the server's identity is not guaranteed. This is common for internal equipment.
rule.tls_self_signed.fix: Acceptable on an internal network; otherwise install a certificate issued by a recognised authority.
rule.tls_self_signed.title: Self-signed certificate (port {port})
rule.upnp.explain: The device advertises its services over UPnP; on a router, UPnP lets any internal device open ports to the Internet.
rule.upnp.fix: Disable UPnP on the router if nothing requires it.
rule.upnp.title: UPnP active
rule.vnc_open.explain: VNC allows viewing and controlling the device's screen; it is often weakly protected or not at all.
rule.vnc_open.fix: Check that a strong password is required, or disable VNC in favour of an encrypted tool.
rule.vnc_open.title: VNC remote control (port {port})
